scenario.name: A captain's trial, the station off Ushant and a stranger

world_orders.order: ship: a brig-sloop "Palinure" of France at 48 44 N 5 20 W, bound for 48 15 N 5 30 W, no colours

scenario.intent: keep the station off Ushant within 15 miles

line.text: The book of standing orders is empty. Begin with none, give your own, or load the starter book: read the standing orders from data/standing_orders/starter.orders (the primer's chapter 11, 'The starting book', gives each routine with its reason).

standing_orders.name: wear at the hour
standing_orders.text: standing order "wear at the hour": every 2 hours, if a stranger in sight is not in sight and the distance to 48 33.3 N 5 26.6 W is under 30 miles then wear ship

standing_orders.name: by the wind
standing_orders.text: standing order "by the wind": at wore then keep her full and by

standing_orders.name: back to the station
standing_orders.text: standing order "back to the station": every watch, if a stranger in sight is not in sight and the distance to 48 33.3 N 5 26.6 W is over 15 miles then shape a course for 48 33.3 N 5 26.6 W

standing_orders.name: a sail on the station
standing_orders.text: standing order "a sail on the station": at a sail sighted then make her out

standing_orders.name: trim to the course
standing_orders.text: standing order "trim to the course": at steady on the course, if the manoeuvre in hand is not hove to then trim sails

standing_orders.name: trim on a shift
standing_orders.text: standing order "trim on a shift": when the true wind veers 1 point or backs 1 point and the manoeuvre in hand is not hove to then trim sails

standing_orders.name: tend the sheets
standing_orders.text: standing order "tend the sheets": every glass, if the manoeuvre in hand is not hove to then trim the sheets

standing_orders.name: bearings
standing_orders.text: standing order "bearings": every glass, if the land is in sight then take a bearing of the land; take a fix

standing_orders.name: the morning sight
standing_orders.text: standing order "the morning sight": at two bells, if the daylight is day then take a sight for the longitude

standing_orders.name: shorten sail for weather
standing_orders.text: standing order "shorten sail for weather": when the true wind exceeds 30 knots for 2 minutes then shorten sail

standing_orders.name: sail after the gale
standing_orders.text: standing order "sail after the gale": when the true wind is under 25 knots for 30 minutes, if the main topsail is reefed then sway up the topgallant masts; shake out the reefs in the topsails; set plain sail
